## Highlights

- A message that carries documents no longer waits for their search index. Each document is read on a worker as soon as it is uploaded, which takes a few seconds, and the message waits for those reads alone; until a document's index is ready, the assistant reads the text that read produced. Before, a message waited until every document in it was indexed, behind every upload queued before it, and two documents in one message could leave it queued for good, its chips at **Indexing…**. Only a document too large to read before it is indexed, or one whose read fails on Tale's side, still holds the message until its indexing finishes: a PDF, Word, PowerPoint or OpenDocument text file over 50 MiB, an Excel workbook over 20 MiB, a text file (CSV included) over 4 MiB, or a file with more than about four million characters of text. The organization's secret scan and PII protection check a read exactly as they check the index, and the checked text stays in the organization's knowledge database until the index completes. A file they refuse, or are still checking, is kept out of everything that takes files (code the assistant runs, a task agent's workspace and an agent review), and a task's brief names it. The chip reads **Reading…**, then the file's size, or why the assistant can't read the file, in your language; keyboard focus opens that reason as well as the pointer. The assistant also receives every attachment's type and size, so a question about a picture's size or format gets an answer instead of a reading step that fails with **Not found**. A message that waited for its attachments now shows its reply without a reload. See [Send while processing continues](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/attachments#send-while-processing-continues).
- A chat filed in a project can answer as one of the project's own agents, with the agent's instructions and equipped skills, and with its model when you may use that model in chat. In a project with agents, a button beside the project in the message box names who answers, one of the agents or **Assistant**, and only the chat's owner can change it; a reply an agent wrote carries the agent's name, and a task made from the chat starts with the chat's agent ([#5361](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5361)). The message box also shows the chat's project: choose one before a new chat's first message, pick another to move the chat, or remove it from its project. A moved chat answers as its new project's default chat agent, and moving a chat shared with its project asks first, because the share ends ([#5362](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5362)). A new chat starts with the project's default chat agent: the first agent created in the project, unless someone who can edit the project (an Editor, Developer, Admin or Owner) chooses another, or **Assistant**, under **Chats** on the project's **General** page ([#5364](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5364)). The assistant can also propose changes to projects and agents: create a project; change a project's name, description, instructions or default chat agent; add an agent; or change an agent's name, instructions, model or skills. It shows the change as a card under its reply, and nothing changes until you select **Apply**. Editors, Developers, Admins and Owners get these proposals in the app ([#5363](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5363)). A project's **Agents** tab now says who can use its agents, and the guide says how to share an agent with the whole organization. See [Choose who answers in a project chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#who-answers), [Create or change projects and agents from chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#proposals) and [Share an agent with everyone](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/project-agents#share-an-agent).
- A person who signed in through single sign-on or an authenticating proxy can now create an API key for themselves under **Settings > API > REST**; such a session was refused with `403 ORG_FORBIDDEN`, whatever the person's role. The sign-in covers one organization, so the key works in that organization only: **Belongs to** reads **You — this organization only**, the key needs no `X-Organization-Slug`, and it shares its holder's rate-limit allowance like every key of theirs. Who may create one is the same rule, read for this organization alone: the Owner, Admin or Developer role here, or a competence an Admin granted here that is used with a key. Owners and Admins can also pick **All keys in this organization**, which adds the personal keys members made after a password sign-in, since those work here too: each is marked **Personal key**, names its holder, and is read-only, because only its holder can revoke it. The create dialog says why the **Member** picker leaves someone out, since it lists only the members below your role, says in one line when the key will not be able to call the organization's model endpoints, and words a refused create in your language. See [Your key after an SSO sign-in](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/api-keys#your-key-after-sso).
- The chat assistant reads a web page's main content, without the site's navigation, header and footer ([#5036](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5036)). A page that builds its content in the browser, or whose site first checks the browser with a script, the challenge of AWS WAF, Cloudflare, Vercel or Fastly, is rendered once in a sandboxed browser, which takes one of the organization's render sessions for a moment and introduces itself as TaleAssistant, with no disguise ([#5183](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5183)). A tender notice on TED, which AWS WAF's challenge kept out on every attempt, reads this way. Tale no longer asks the next outbound proxy for a page that answered with a CAPTCHA: only a challenge is asked for again, and a CAPTCHA or a refusal is reported at once and never opened in the browser. Nothing is ever solved: a check that waits for a person in the browser, as a Cloudflare check can, reads nothing. A failed reading step now says why, in your language, where it read **Failed** and its details held an English message: no page at the address, a site that keeps automated readers out, a CAPTCHA, a check the browser did not get past, no browser free, a site that didn't answer in time. A website crawl whose browser meets a bot check it gets past now stores the page behind it, where it failed the page as "HTTP 403 at render time"; a page whose plain request the site already answers with a check still fails. Every request of a rendered page, a crawl's included, now goes through the sandbox's egress proxy, so a page's scripts can no longer reach the sandbox network's own services. See [Check what the assistant used](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#check-what-the-assistant-used) and, for each reason a page can't be read, [Improve an incomplete answer](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#improve-an-incomplete-answer).
- A presentation the **pptx** skill builds from a corporate template keeps the template's sections in step with its slides. Before, the sections kept listing the template slides the deck no longer had, and the new slides sat in none, so PowerPoint showed every template section as empty, "(0)", beside the generated slides. Now a section the deleted template slides leave empty goes, a new slide joins the section of the slide before it, and a section of your own deck that was already empty stays. The skill deletes a slide through its own script, which takes the slide out of its section and keeps the deck's slide files unique, and its QA checks every section against the slides it holds. Organizations that already exist keep the pptx skill they were created with; see the Upgrade notes.
- Personal data masking now catches IBANs in the backend. The IBAN check failed on every IBAN there, so an organization whose PII protection covers IBANs had none masked, tokenized or blocked: not in chat messages, not in requests to its model endpoints, not in indexed documents and emails, and not in attachments read for the assistant. This held for every 0.5 release before this one; see the Upgrade notes about what was stored and indexed before. See [Protect personal data](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/guardrails#protect-personal-data).
- A long chat keeps the full results of the assistant's earlier steps while the conversation fits the model's context window. Before, a follow-up after a turn that read web pages sent every earlier result cut to 400 characters, and a model such as Claude Sonnet 5.5 opened its next reply by correcting an answer that was right and fetching the pages again. When a conversation no longer fits, the oldest results are shortened first, each with a note that the answer after it was written from the whole result, and the oldest messages are left out only when that is not enough ([#5356](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5356)). See [Continue, copy, or keep the conversation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#continue-copy-or-keep-the-conversation).
- A file a reply made shows once, under the reply. A model that also wrote the file's reference into its text drew the file a second time, as a grey placeholder whose preview opened empty; now a link to a stored file in the text opens its preview, and a picture that can't be drawn reads as its description ([#5358](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5358)). A picture or preview opened more than 15 minutes after its page loaded showed a broken image, because its link had run out; Tale now fetches a new link when one no longer loads, for the pictures under a reply, a message's attached photos and a task's pictures ([#5366](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5366)). See [Open and download the files](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/files-and-skills#open-and-download-the-files).
- A sandbox session on a slow Docker host has the rest of its startup budget, `SANDBOX_SESSION_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 seconds by default), to start its container, where the start was cut off after 30 seconds and failed with an empty error. A start that runs out of time names the timeout and the variable that sets it ([#5280](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5280)).
- Also fixed: a member reading a chat shared with its project no longer makes requests only the chat's owner may make, which filled the browser console with 404 errors, and sees a reply that is still being written once it is finished ([#5383](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5383)); screen readers read a project's name once where its icon stands beside it ([#5382](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5382)); file previews and Markdown code blocks highlight CSV and the other languages outside the 39 loaded up front ([#5384](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5384)); and the Session Manager opens an empty list on its empty state instead of a flicker of placeholder rows, draws its frame before its scripts load, and passes a tunnel's whole answer to a browser that reads it slowly, where the answer could end short ([#5387](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5387)).

## Upgrade notes

- From v0.5.100 to v0.5.101 the backend applies three migrations to the application database at start, each safe while the previous image still serves:
  - `0236_chat_agents.sql` adds the agent a chat answers as (`chat_agent_id` on `app.thread_metadata`) and a project's default chat agent (`default_chat_agent_id` and `chats_start_with_assistant` on `app.projects`). Chats from before the upgrade keep the assistant.
  - `0237_chat_proposals.sql` adds `app.chat_proposals`, which keeps the changes a chat proposed and what applying them did.
  - `0238_file_metadata_text_reads.sql` adds where a document's read stands (`text_status`, `text_error_code` and `text_read_at_ms` on `app.file_metadata`) and an index of the reads still under way.
- The knowledge database gets `00000000000020_document_reads.sql` in its `private_knowledge` schema: the table `private_knowledge.document_reads`, which keeps a read document's checked text until its index completes, or for as long as the file when it is not indexed. The `knowledge-db` service applies it when it starts, and so does the worker; an organization's own knowledge database gets it on first use. Until it is there, a read is deferred and its message waits for the document's index, as before, and removing deleted files from the knowledge database, an organization's teardown and the nightly reconcile fail and are retried.
- The API contract stays at `3.52.0`. Over the REST API, a message to a chat that answers as one of its project's agents in the app, whether its owner chose it or the chat started with the project's default, is answered by that agent, and the message reads do not name it; a chat the API creates answers as the assistant, also in a project whose new chats start with an agent.
- In a project that has agents of its own, new chats now start with the project's first agent instead of the assistant. To keep the assistant, someone who can edit the project (an Editor, Developer, Admin or Owner) chooses **Assistant** as the **Default chat agent** under **Chats** on the project's **General** page.
- Content stored or indexed before the upgrade under a PII protection that masks, tokenizes or blocks IBANs holds its IBANs as written: the protection passed over them. **Reindex** in a document's row menu under **Knowledge > Documents** indexes it again under the protection, up to ten a minute per person; do this for the documents that may hold IBANs. Nothing in the app indexes again a file already indexed in a project's **Knowledge** tab, a chat attachment, or an email or its attachments, and saving the PII protection settings does not either; only moving the organization to another embedding model indexes everything again. Chat messages sent before the upgrade keep their IBANs and go to the model again with their chat's history. What the model already received is not changed.
- Organizations that already exist keep the pptx skill they were created with, so they do not get the section fixes by themselves ([#4964](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4964)). To give one the new skill, an Owner or Admin uploads this release's `configs/platform/custom/skills/pptx` folder under **Settings > Skills** with **Add skill > Upload folder** and replaces the existing **pptx** when asked; the upload makes them the skill's creator, so it no longer reads **Built-in**. An operator can instead copy `/app/builtin/skills/pptx` from the new platform image over the organization's `skills/pptx` folder in its configuration directory. `tale deploy --override-all` also does it, but it implies `--stop`, which restarts the database, object store and proxy, and it resets every built-in file of every organization, governance policies such as PII protection included.
- A Release run no longer refuses a second version on the same UTC day: a version goes out whenever it is needed. Releases still publish one at a time, and none is cancelled mid-flight. Upgrade a version's service images and its CLI together, as before.
- No configuration, limit, credential or sign-in setting needs to change beyond these: the other fixes take effect with the new images.
